summary: Backpressure propagation causing 5xx spike and runtime crash-loop for tenant Voyant Health
description:
Issue summary: Customer (Voyant Health) observed a sudden elevation in 5xx errors beginning ~2026-03-10T18:20Z on their dedicated tenant. The spike correlated with throughput collapse and repeated upstream runtime process exits. Impact: production traffic for Voyant's inference endpoints experienced increased latency, intermittent failed requests (5xx), and degraded availability for a subset of traffic patterns (largely streaming chat and long-context requests). Estimated affected requests: ~12% of requests to their tenant during the 45-minute window.

Environment: Dedicated pool (voyant-dedicated-us-east), API Gateway fronting serving-runtime pool, autoscaler configured with warm pool and scale-up thresholds.

Initial customer report: Voyant ops reported repeated 502/503 responses and client-observed session drops. They provided sample request IDs and timestamps which are attached in comments.

Urgency: High — P0 due to customer-facing availability degradation during business hours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send sustained concurrent streaming chat requests that keep KV cache warm and long prompt lengths (>4k tokens) to Voyant tenant endpoints.
2) Observe accept queue latencies at APIGW rising above 300ms and downstream runtime connection churn.
3) After sustained ingress, API Gateway begins returning 502/503 and serving-runtime processes restart due to watchdog triggers.
4) Reproduce more reliably when autoscaler is near its scale-up threshold and warm worker pool is partially filled.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10T18:30Z - Support triage: Verified customer request IDs; reproduced elevated 5xx from our staging loadgen by sending similar long-context streams to dedicated tenant (match).
2026-03-10T18:45Z - SRE: Observed accept queue latencies spiking at APIGW; proxy backlog growth correlates with runtime connection churn and worker restarts.
2026-03-10T19:02Z - Runtime team: Noted repeated KV cache allocations and occasional large allocations leading to runtime OOM watchdogs when prefetch/pinning overlaps with autoscaler events.

2026-03-10T19:20Z - Hypothesis: Backpressure from slow runtime startup paths and large KV cache warms propagates into APIGW accept queues; the accept queue growth triggers client timeouts, which cause retry amplification and further load, producing a positive feedback loop culminating in runtime crash-loop.
2026-03-11T09:15Z - Observed that autoscaler added workers slowly due to conservative cooldown and warm-pool sizing; scale-up lag allowed backlog to cross runtime watchdog thresholds.

2026-03-11T11:50Z - Confirmed that affected traffic pattern is long streaming sessions that simultaneously keep KV caches warm and request model hot-swap behavior (preferred by Voyant), increasing memory pressure and long GC pauses on some runtime instances.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10T18:35Z: Received initial report from Voyant. Collected request IDs: req_3f9a, req_7b2c, req_9d4f. Customer notes 40% error increase during 18:20-19:00 UTC.
Lena Fischer (SRE) 2026-03-10T18:50Z: We see accept queue growth on apigw-01/02; routing shows several runtime processes cycling. Investigating runtime OOM/hangs and autoscaler logs.

Marco Hernandez (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-10T19:10Z: Runtime process logs show large KV cache allocations and occasional allocation spikes correlated to model prefetch. Adding memory guard/early eviction could mitigate. Will prepare patch for non-blocking eviction.
Voyant Ops (Customer) 2026-03-10T19:22Z: Thank you — we can throttle our client to 60 concurrent streams as a workaround if that helps while you investigate.

Lena Fischer (SRE) 2026-03-10T19:35Z: Applying temporary mitigations: 1) Cap concurrent streams for Voyant tenant at APIGW to 75, 2) Increase runtime watchdog timeout by 30s, 3) Bump autoscaler aggressiveness for this pool to reduce scale-up lag. Monitoring impact.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-11T12:05Z: Customer confirms error rate reduced to baseline after mitigations; still seeing occasional spikes under sustained load. Planning RCA and long-term fix.
Marco Hernandez (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-11T14:40Z: Pushed non-blocking KV eviction prototype to staging for validation; PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8912 referenced below.
resolution: Temporary mitigations applied: tenant-level concurrent stream cap, increased runtime watchdog timeout, and autoscaler scale-up tuning. Immediate customer impact reduced to baseline. Root cause appears to be backpressure amplification between APIGW accept queues and serving-runtime when long-context streaming workload overlaps with KV cache warm/prefetch and conservative autoscaler cooldowns. Follow-up actions: Roll out non-blocking KV eviction patch, adjust autoscaler warm-pool heuristics, add accept-queue throttling safeguards, and author an RCA doc. Postmortem scheduled.
